forecaster_note: There'll be a little bit of leftover SE swell and some more mid-long period S swell than showing on the spot forecasts. Don't expect it to be big. I only think we'll see 2-3ft of longer S swell so surf will likely be about chest high at south exposures, maybe with the odd bigger set. Enough to get going though. Pretty small elsewhere, but rideable on floaty boards. Clean and sunny all day with offshores. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: Light W offshore 9 gusting 11 km/h — glassy all morning, easing further by midday

shark.summary: No shark detections or sightings logged Palm Beach → Manly in the last 24h. Most recent Northern Beaches notification was ~9 days ago (Long Reef / Dee Why drone sightings).

days.label: Today
days.note: Small and clean — 12 kJ is barely a pulse, so this is a longboard/fish morning, not a shortboard one. Light W offshore holds all day and the tide fills from a 5:43am low to a 12:04pm high, so mid-morning is the only window worth the drive. Curl Curl and Long Reef are picking up marginally more of the leftover SE than Dee Why.

dee-why.window: 9–11am on the pushing tide. Rated FAIR through 9am then drops to poor-fair as the tide floods to 1.43m at noon.

tip.label: Point vs beachie
tip.text: At 12 kJ the Point won't have enough push to wrap and stand up — you'll be paddling more than surfing. Take the beachies at the north end on the incoming tide and treat it as a tune-up, frontside on any right that shows.

long-reef.window: Best size on the coast today (1–3ft) but rated only poor-fair — worth a look 9–10am if Dee Why is flat.

tip.label: Size over quality
tip.text: Long Reef holds the biggest numbers today purely from exposure. Wind goes cross by noon here while Dee Why stays offshore, so go early or don't bother.

curl-curl.window: Pick of the four — FAIR to 9am with 1–3ft. Go 8:30–10:30am before the high tide fattens the banks.

tip.label: Best of a small day
tip.text: Curl Curl is the only spot combining FAIR rating with the bigger 1–3ft numbers. South corner banks handle the SSW windswell best; expect short, fast lefts — backside for you, so drive off the bottom early.

manly.window: Skip unless you're already in town — smallest of the four, poor-fair all day.

tip.label: Log it
tip.text: North Steyne is the shadow spot on a SSW windswell. If you're stuck here it's a longboard-only session on the incoming tide.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Energy nearly doubles to 23 kJ but the wind turns against you — W offshore builds to 15 km/h gusting 33 by 9am. Still small at 1–2ft. Watch the new 1.6ft @ 10s ENE (88°) in the mix: that's the leading edge of the swell that fills in for the weekend.

dee-why.window: Dawn only. Gusts hit 33 km/h by 9am and it's poor-fair all day regardless.

long-reef.window: 6–7am FAIR, then drops off. Late arvo (3pm) climbs back to FAIR as the wind eases.

curl-curl.window: Dawn or 3pm. Same FAIR bookends as Long Reef with the midday slump between.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: This is the one to plan for. Saturday: 82 kJ but the swell is dead S (181° @ 9s) — it wraps badly into Dee Why, so Long Reef and Curl Curl (2–4ft, FAIR all day) are the calls. Sunday is the standout: 143 kJ from a 4.3ft @ 9s ENE (52–62°) — exactly the direction Dee Why wants. Catch is the NNW wind: offshore at 6am, cross by 9am, 20 gusting 37 km/h by noon. Sunday dawn to 9am is the session of the week.

dee-why.window: Sat: FAIR to 9am then degrades to POOR by 3pm — dead S swell doesn't wrap here. Sun: get on it at first light; ENE 52° finally lines the Point up but the NNW goes cross by 9am.
alerts: Sat swell is dead S (181°) — poor wrap into Dee Why
Sun wind 20 gusting 37 km/h NNW from midday

tip.label: Sunday dawn, Point
tip.text: 143 kJ on a 9–10s ENE at 52–62° is the best combination you'll see all week and it's the one direction Dee Why Point actually likes. Frontside rights, 6–8:30am, before the NNW swings cross-shore. If you only surf once this week, make it this.

long-reef.window: Best of the weekend both days. Sat FAIR all day at 2–4ft; Sun FAIR-GOOD at 6am and 9am, 3–4ft.
alerts: Sun wind 20 gusting 37 km/h NNW from midday

tip.label: The safe bet
tip.text: Long Reef is the only spot rated FAIR-GOOD this week and it handles both the Saturday S and the Sunday ENE. If Sunday's NNW is already up when you look out the window, this is the fallback — the headland gives it more shelter than Dee Why.

curl-curl.window: Sat 2–4ft, FAIR to 9am then fades to POOR by 3pm. Sun FAIR all day, 2–4ft — the most consistent rating of the weekend.
alerts: Sun wind 20 gusting 37 km/h NNW from midday

manly.window: Sat FAIR early at 1–3ft, Sun poor-fair at 2–3ft. Bottom of the list both days.
